title: A general differential split-sample test to select sub-periods of discontinuous years gathering similar to different climate conditions
author: Dakhlaoui, Ruelland, et al.
materials: The arguments of the routine are:
The code give the following outputs:

steps.title: Prepare input data file
steps.instruction: Create a MATLAB file named PTfile.mat containing a matrix PT with dimensions years × (2 × number_of_catchments + 1). Column 1 holds the hydrological year (e.g., 1971–2000 for the reference period 1 Sep 1970 – 31 Aug 2000). For each catchment, two successive columns store annual precipitation and mean annual temperature. Ensure the reference period includes l = 30 hydrological years.

steps.title: Place code files together
steps.instruction: Copy the files PTfile.mat, SST.m, and MainSST.m into the same working folder so that the MATLAB scripts can locate the data and functions.

steps.title: Configure SST parameters
steps.instruction: Edit SST.m (or set variables before running) to define: • OptSST = 'GDSST' to select the General Differential Split‑Sample Test; • nsousperiod = k (the desired number of calibration sub‑periods); • durationSubP = n (the length of each sub‑period in years); • AnnualPrecip and AnnualTemp as 2 × l arrays (year column and variable column).

steps.title: Run main script
steps.instruction: Execute MainSST.m in MATLAB. The script reads PTfile.mat, passes the defined variables to SST.m, and initiates the GDSST algorithm.

steps.title: Generate one sub‑period
steps.instruction: Follow steps 1‑5 of the GDSST to build a single n‑year calibration sub‑period:

substeps.instruction: 1. Randomly pick the first year of the sub‑period from the l hydrological years (step 1).

2. Compute the Mahalanobis distance of each of the remaining l‑1 years to the selected year in the two‑dimensional climate space (mean annual temperature T and total annual precipitation P). This rescales the axes to unit variance and accounts for correlation (step 2).
3. Sort the l‑1 years by increasing Mahalanobis distance. Randomly choose an integer m from the interval [n‑1, l‑1] (step 3).

4. Assign a trapezoidal probability to the sorted years: for rank i = 1…m, P(i) = 2 · (m + 1 − i) / [m · (m + 1)]; for i > m, P(i) = 0 (step 3 formula). The closest year (i = 1) thus has probability P(1) = 2/(m + 1).

5. Randomly select n‑1 years from the l‑1 candidates according to the probabilities P(i) (step 4). Only the m closest years have a non‑zero chance, favouring similar climate but allowing contrast because m varies each iteration.

6. Assemble the n years (the first randomly chosen year plus the n‑1 selected years) into a candidate sub‑period. If this exact set of years has already been generated, discard it and return to step 1 (step 5).

steps.title: Repeat until enough sub‑periods
steps.instruction: Iterate the “Generate one sub‑period” procedure until the required number k (sub‑periods) is obtained (step 7).

steps.title: Define validation exercises
steps.instruction: For each generated calibration sub‑period, consider any n‑year period that shares no year with the calibration period as an independent validation exercise. Record calibration‑validation pairs, ΔT (temperature difference) and ΔP (precipitation difference) as produced by the routine.
